Greetings, seeker of knowledge. I am the Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, and you have asked to peer into the shadowed records concerning the Forest of Wyrms. Unroll the maps of the Western Heartlands, and let us delve into the dark and venom-choked history of this ancient wood.

### Geographic Overview

The Forest of Wyrms is a dark, brooding, and incredibly dense woodland nestled in the Western Heartlands. It is situated south of the Winding Water river, east of the Trade Way near the settlement of Soubar, and west of the Trielta Hills. The woods are defined by their soaring, ancient redwoods and thick pines, with some majestic trunks measuring more than twenty feet in diameter. 

Beneath the dense canopy, the air is perennially cool, damp, and cloaked in clinging mists. Navigating the forest floor is relatively unobstructed; the terrain is surprisingly smooth and devoid of thick underbrush, save for large, dense patches of jagged helmthorn brush. Sages of Candlekeep postulate that the colossal height of the trees and the unnatural vigor of the woods are lingering manifestations of high elven magic, a remnant from when the forest was a part of the ancient elven empire of Shantel Othreier. Attempting to log the forest is considered a fool's errand, not merely because of the rocky surroundings, but due to the lethal flora and fauna that call the shadows home.

### Flora, Fauna, and the Emerald Tyrants

The forest derives its name from its most infamous apex predators: green dragons. The woodland serves as a prime nesting and hunting ground for a large population of immature and ancient green wyrms. Many of the forest's scaled tyrants are direct descendants of the legendary green dragon Agyrtclughwaur, who historically ruled its depths. Today, the southern and eastern reaches of the forest are fiercely guarded by mature green dragons such as Ralionate and Rylatar'ralah'tyma. Curiously, the forest is also home to Tharas'kalagram, a red dragon who lairs within the caldera of a small, localized volcano.

Beyond the dragons, the forest floor writhes with serpentine life. When the yuan-ti migrated to this region millennia ago, they brought with them—and magically bred—countless species of deadly snakes. Unwary travelers are frequently hunted by jaculis, massive tree pythons, and venomous deathcoils. The deeper reaches are also guarded by sword spiders, bone dark nagas, and ti-khana dinosaurs.

### Historical Overview and Notable Ruins

The history of the Forest of Wyrms is inextricably linked to Najara, the Kingdom of Snakes. Long before the founding of human cities on the Sword Coast, this region was a major hub of the sarrukh—the progenitor creator race of the scaled kind. 

**Ss'thar'tiss'ssun:** Deep in the northern fringes of the forest lies the ruins of Ss'thar'tiss'ssun, one of the oldest archaeological sites in all of Faerûn. Originally built by the sarrukh, the city was later rebuilt by ophidians and yuan-ti to serve as the capital of Najara. In the Year of the Moor Birds (90 DR), Netherese wizards in the employ of the Shadowking leveled the city, driving the yuan-ti north into the Serpent Hills. Today, the ruins house the Shrine of the Cowled Serpents, and the site remains a deeply sacred destination for yuan-ti pilgrims. 

**Ss'kowlyn'raa:** In the Year of the Grimoire (1354 DR), yuan-ti wizards known as the Coiled Cabal established this settlement in the southern reaches of the forest. Built within a deep, overgrown ravine lined with caves, Ss'kowlyn'raa serves as a subterranean academy for dark magical inquiry, entirely linked by magic-hewn tunnels that eventually connect back to the Serpent Hills.

**Thlohtzin:** This dark citadel was once the fortress of a powerful lich. After it was left abandoned, it was claimed by the yuan-ti and repurposed into a crucial stronghold for Najara's slave trade. Its strategic location commands the routes between the Serpent Hills and the Zhentarim fortress of Darkhold, making it a hub of illicit and highly lucrative commerce.

**Lyran's Hold:** Situated on the western edge of the wood, this formidable, magically warded tower was erected by a wizard named Lyran, who eventually succumbed to the dark arts and became a lich. Though courageous adventurers and Harpers eventually slew the undead lord, tragic rumors suggest that the very heroes who claimed the keep eventually inherited the lich's evil ways, falling to the insidious corruption of the forest.

Heed this warning, traveler: as recorded in our most solemn tomes, only a fool enters the Forest of Wyrms intentionally. If the venom of the serpent does not claim your life, the acidic breath of the forest's true masters surely will.
